text:
Young musicians completing a year of intensive orchestral training will take center stage Nov. 28 as the Korean National Symphony Orchestra (KNSO) presents its KNSO Academy concert, "Soar," marking the end of their training and the beginning of their professional musical careers.
The concert, scheduled for 5 p.m. at Sejong Arts Center, brings together young musicians who have spent a year developing their performance skills through practical training, mentoring and regular orchestral performances.
Since its launch in 2021, the academy has trained 109 musicians, 49 of whom have joined major Korean orchestras, including KBS Symphony Orchestra, Gyeonggi Philharmonic Orchestra and Daejeon Philharmonic Orchestra, representing an employment rate of approximately 45 percent.
The program opens with the world premiere of "And, Overture" (2026), a newly commissioned work by composer No Jae-bong, who previously served as composer-in-residence for the National Symphony Orchestra.
The piece explores the idea that every ending carries the possibility of another beginning, reflecting the young musicians' transition from training to professional performance.
Pianist Hyo Lee will then join the orchestra for Edvard Grieg's Piano Concerto in A minor, Op. 16. Lee won third prize at the 2025 Long-Thibaud International Competition and advanced to the semifinals of the 19th International Chopin Piano Competition.
The concert will conclude with Robert Schumann's Symphony No. 4 in C minor, Op. 120, a work whose four movements flow continuously into one another.
Belgian conductor Martijn Dendievel will lead the performance. He won the 2021 German Conducting Award and has conducted orchestras including the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra and London Symphony Orchestra.
Tickets cost 40,000 won ($28), 20,000 won and 10,000 won, depending on seating.
